item.title: Dev Log 1: Introduction to Project Vertex
item.description:
Dearest Community,

Rustling Leaves Games was built on a vision, a dream where people can come together and build something beautiful. A group of like-minded individuals with full-time jobs, willing to pour sweat and tears into building a game that proves we are so much more than a number tossed to the side of a stack of papers on a recruiter’s desk or a name at the start of a gut-wrenching Human Resources layoff email. Our vision is a community-built game called Project Vertex.

item.title: Dev Log 2: Introduction the Trotson Radio
item.description:
Dearest Community,

We are so excited to announce the Trotson game mechanic, which will be featured in our upcoming game, Project Vertex. The Trotson radio is a handheld radio offering a variety of sounds from radio stations and mixtapes to let players rest their minds, sit back, and enjoy music. As you play the game, you will also discover mixtapes scattered across the world, each telling stories hidden behind powerful songs and even more powerful memories.

item.title: 2D Concept Artists (Characters & Environments)
item.description:
< Back to Listing

Rustling Leaves Games is an indie studio focused on creating emotional, narrative-driven interactive experiences. We’re a small, collaborative team building thoughtful and atmospheric games, and we’re looking for 2D Concept Artists (Characters & Environments) to help define the mood, tone, and visuals of our environments and characters.

Role Overview
#

As a 2D Concept Artist, you will be responsible for creating visually compelling character and/or environment designs that define the look and feel of our world. Your work will serve as the foundation for 3D production, ensuring assets are both artistically strong and technically translatable, while supporting the project’s overall narrative and emotional tone.

You’ll work closely with designers, writers, and other developers to implement features such as dialog systems, inventory systems (if needed), save/load functionality, UI systems, and other gameplay tools that help shape our world.

Rustling Leaves Games is looking for a Graphic Designer to help bring our game and studio brand to life visually.

We’re looking for someone who can create:

You’ll work closely with our development and creative teams to make sure our visual identity feels cohesive, memorable, and true to the heart of our games.

item.title: Dev Log 3: Sculpting Words: Narrative Design of Project Vertex
item.description:
Dearest Community,

Our narrative journey began with a short paragraph describing Project Vertex, lost within a 20-page Game Development Document (GDD). At the time, we only knew two things about Project Vertex: that it was a role-playing game where the players could affect the outcomes of the story, and that the story meant everything to the game. We wanted to make players laugh, be curious, and experience a sense of familiarity. What started as a paragraph has since turned into a document all of its own, called the Narrative Bible. This document outlines a breakdown of every episode, act, and scene within our game. Some things were easy to decide; nature showcases four seasons, so each episode is based on a new season. Acts are moments within the Episode. Scenes are the played-out scripts within the act itself. We quickly realized we were going to be overwhelmed with the sheer amount of work that it takes to write out a story. Without a story, you cannot create concept art; without concept art, there are no assets; without assets, you can’t whitebox game mechanics.

item.title: Dev Log 4: Words Into Art: The Concept Art Process
item.description:
Dearest Community,

How do we translate words into art? That is the age-old question we ask ourselves every day at Rustling Leaves Games!

Our concept art process begins with a character or environmental description; we call it a profile. The profile defines the character’s emotional tone, descriptive factors, and personality traits. That, coupled with the entire narrative design, allows us to create something truly amazing!

item.title: Dev Log 5: What’s in a Name: Choosing Our Game Title
item.description:
“The most expensive marketing mistake might happen before your game even has a logo.”
- Maria Amirkhanyan

Dearest Community,

Naming is one of the earliest product decisions devs encounter, yet it’s often based on brainstorming sessions and internal votes.

At Rustling Leaves Games, we’ve decided to treat it like any other product decision: define reasons, validate them with real-life players, and make the final choice using evidence rather than intuition. Of course we would have a biased opinion; we’re the ones making the game!

About Us

Together, we build heartfelt, immersive experiences that let players step into unfamiliar lives, explore deeper truths, and feel part of something bigger.
How It All Started
Our studio started with one BIG idea: what if we built an indie game studio of artists, developers, and musicians who work on a shared project where transparency and flexibility aren’t optional-they’re the standard. A studio where moms, recent layoffs, veterans, and entry-level people who are willing to learn together, make decisions together, and share responsibility can lean on each other and build on our collective strengths. This studio was created for people who are willing to learn, step outside their comfort zone, and try something new while being supported by an entire team.
The Games We Create
We believe games aren’t just played; they are inspiring. When players sit on a park bench in our game to just sit in the music playing in the background and think about the story, we want them to feel the care we’ve poured into every part of every episode; who knows, maybe we can even inspire you to think differently. In a world where it’s easier to be hateful, we don’t want to have to explain to you what the right choice is, we want you to come up with your own conclusions, see the actions you choose have real-time consequences, and hopefully our games can make you explore deeper truths.
The Feels We Stir
Our games are deeply human at their core. We put in the research: where is a character from? What music do they like? What makes them “human”? We want players to feel connected to our stories in their own way. Our worlds are built from familiar places, familiar feelings, small moments that carry weight, shaped by time and lived history. Step into our characters’ shoes and experience something recognizable, even in the extraordinary.
A United Team With A Vision
We are a collective force, shaped by leadership teams, big ideas, and the ability to listen to each other objectively, while still walking the same path. Directions change, but the vision remains. We are a team that cares deeply, builds intentionally, and lives honestly. In a world where entry-level gaming industry jobs are muddled with layoffs, poor leadership, and siloed ideas, we are shaking up the industry and investing in our own future.
